facts.title: ThAME: 3D Memory-Enabled Heterogeneous Accelerator for LLM Mixture of Experts
facts.event_hint: ThAME: a proposed 3D heterogeneous multi-chiplet accelerator combining FeFET-NAND and DRAM memory chiplets with a co-designed hierarchical NoC for MoE LLM inference (architecture study, not silicon).
facts.problem: MoE inference on conventional hardware is bottlenecked by three issues: massive memory bandwidth needed to fetch non-contiguous expert weights, non-deterministic scatter-gather traffic from input-dependent token routing, and tail-latency dependency from synchronous expert output aggregation. Expert weights dominate model size (>90%) and existing memory hierarchies cannot balance density, leakage and access latency.
facts.mechanism: ThAME is a 3D heterogeneous multi-chiplet architecture using FeFET (ferroelectric FET) non-volatile and DRAM volatile memory chiplets with a co-designed compute mapping that aligns attention and expert routing profiles. It stores expert weights on-chip in 3D FeFET-NAND to break the memory wall, and adds a specialized hierarchical Network-on-Chip (designed via Archived Multi-Objective Simulated Annealing, AMOSA) inside the FeFET-NAND die to mitigate non-deterministic token-routing traffic. Evaluated config: two FeFET and two DRAM memory chiplets plus a systolic-array (TPU v6e) host chiplet on a silicon interposer, point-to-point connected.

evidence.claim: ThAME outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts by up to 15.7x speedup and improves energy efficiency by up to 9.8x.
evidence.value: up to 15.7x speedup; up to 9.8x energy efficiency
evidence.condition: abstract headline; detailed baseline/workload in results
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: ThAME delivers 147.5 Tokens/s/W, a 5.6x, 20.9x and 31.7x improvement over Stratum, TPU v6e and NVIDIA A100 baselines respectively; normalized by silicon area it reaches 184.3 Tokens/s/kW/mm^2.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13

evidence.claim: At batch size B=64 (Deepseek model, MMLU), ThAME delivers up to 5.92x and 12.77x higher throughput than Stratum and H3D-T respectively; the gap widens with batch size due to Stratum/H3D-T network contention.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Scalability

evidence.claim: Co-design decomposition: swapping ThAME's hierarchical NoC for a Mesh topology degrades latency up to 1.44x and energy efficiency up to 2.1x; substituting FeFET-NAND with DRAM-PNM adds up to 1.8x energy overhead; synergistic co-design yields 4.7x/7.0x latency and 5.4x/8.7x energy efficiency gains over Stratum for Qwen1.5 and Deepseek respectively.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 11

evidence.claim: Evaluation uses cycle-accurate simulators: SCALE-Sim for systolic array latency (median error <3% vs production TPU), NeuroSim for FeFET-NAND 3D arrays (chip-level error <1% after calibration), BookSim2 for intra-chiplet NoC, HotSpot for thermal; 16-bit fixed-point precision; MoE models Deepseek-16B, Olmoe-1B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, Qwen3-30B and dense Llama3-8B.
evidence.condition: 45C ambient, 50W base die budget, 4096 PEs/core, 32-core system, 121mm^2 base die
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 8 - Experimental Setup

facts.evaluation_context: Architecture study evaluated entirely via cycle-accurate simulation (SCALE-Sim, NeuroSim, BookSim2, HotSpot), not taped-out silicon. 16-bit fixed-point precision. Config: 2 FeFET + 2 DRAM chiplets + TPU v6e host on silicon interposer, 32-core/4096-PE system, 121mm^2 base die, 50W base-die thermal budget at 45C ambient. Baselines: Stratum (DRAM-PNM), H3D-T (3D FeFET/SRAM/TPU), TPU v6e, NVIDIA A100. MoE workloads: Deepseek-16B, Olmoe-1B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, Qwen3-30B; dense Llama3-8B.
facts.limitations: Results are simulation-based (cycle-accurate modeling, calibrated but not silicon measurements); no real chip, no deployment. HBF reference (SK Hynix H^3 up to 2.69x throughput-per-watt) is cited as related context, not a ThAME measurement. The evaluated chiplet count/config is one specific point; authors note it does not affect generalizability but other configs are not shown. Decode-phase token latency and end-to-end serving P95 are not reported; metrics focus on speedup, energy efficiency, Tokens/s/W and throughput scaling. FeFET device variability/endurance is acknowledged as a memory-technology trade-off but not quantified in results.
facts.project_relevance: ThAME directly addresses the MoE memory-wall and intra-chiplet routing problem relevant to AI accelerator architecture and memory-IO codesign: it couples high-density 3D FeFET-NAND storage with a specialized NoC. For the project card it is a simulation-stage architecture proposal (not pre-silicon validation or production), so its system claims are architectural projections rather than measured silicon. The HBF/FeFET angle also touches the storage-media question of whether NAND-based near-memory compute can enter the AI memory hierarchy.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.17074v2 (19 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source.
All performance numbers come from cycle-accurate simulation (SCALE-Sim/NeuroSim/BookSim2/HotSpot), not silicon.
Baselines are explicitly named: Stratum, H3D-T, TPU v6e, NVIDIA A100.

facts.title: D-NOVA: In-Storage Retrieval Accelerator via Dual-Bound 3D NAND-Optimized Similarity Search with Vector Adaptation
facts.event_hint: D-NOVA: an in-storage vector retrieval accelerator for RAG that embeds IVF-based similarity search directly into 3D NAND arrays using Dual-bound Tight Similarity Sensing (DTS) and a contrastive vector adapter (MICRO 2026).
facts.problem: Dense vector retrieval in RAG is the primary latency/energy bottleneck. Existing in-storage/near-storage accelerators (SmartSSD, RAGX, REIS) still rely on host/embedded processors for final re-ranking; in REIS this INT8 re-ranking step accounts for nearly 70% of total retrieval time, dominated by multi-level cell read latency and data movement to the embedded processor, creating a new memory wall.
facts.mechanism: D-NOVA executes an IVF-based hierarchical retrieval pipeline entirely inside the NAND array. It introduces Dual-bound Tight Similarity Sensing (DTS), a distance metric that reformulates vector retrieval as a query-dependent threshold search over ordered V_TH levels using complement sensing and compact scoring within the NAND string. A lightweight contrastive adapter maps embedding vectors into a DTS-friendly domain to recover near-software recall. Only compact scores/metadata leave the array; full embeddings never move off-array. D-NOVA reuses existing page-buffer structures in binary pass/fail mode, preserving standard QLC read/program compatibility and achieving SLC-like read latency at QLC density.

evidence.claim: D-NOVA is up to 41.7x faster and 71x more energy-efficient than a CPU baseline, and achieves 12.13x higher throughput while being up to 1.26x more energy-efficient than state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators.
evidence.baseline: CPU baseline; state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators
evidence.condition: abstract headline; per-workload breakdown in results
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: In prior in-storage accelerators, the off-array INT8 re-ranking step accounts for nearly 70% of total retrieval time, dominated by MLC read latency and data movement to the embedded processor.
evidence.condition: REIS-style in-storage accelerators with controller-side re-ranking
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 2 - REIS analysis

evidence.claim: D-NOVA and D-NOVA-F sustain roughly 481-679x of the CPU QPS and about 42.7-67.9x of the NSP baseline throughput; relative to REIS, D-NOVA/D-NOVA-F improve throughput by ~4.3-6.1x and D-NOVA-XF reaches ~8.6-12.1x higher QPS.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12 - Throughput Improvement

evidence.claim: Compared to REIS, D-NOVA reduces latency by 3.01-3.79x, D-NOVA-F by 3.80-4.99x, and D-NOVA-XF by 5.98-7.53x, with additional energy savings of 6-27% by avoiding off-array final re-ranking.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12

evidence.claim: Simulated on QLC 3D NAND (128 WLs/string, 8.5V window, PTM-MG 14nm) using Spectre circuit simulation and Monte Carlo V_TH variation modeling; config: PCIe 4.0x4 host, 8 flash channels (16 GB/s total), 8 dies/ch, 12 planes/die, ~1 TB/s inter-plane H-Tree bandwidth; shared accumulator adds 0.023 mm^2/plane (<1.5% of 1.476 mm^2 plane area) synthesized at ASAP7 7nm.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 9 - Tables 1 & 2; PDF Page 12 - 6.7 Overhead

facts.evaluation_context: Simulated in-storage NVMe SSD subsystem (not silicon). QLC 3D NAND (128 WLs/string), 8 flash channels at 2.0 GB/s/channel (16 GB/s total), 8 dies/channel, 12 planes/die, ~1 TB/s inter-plane H-Tree bandwidth, PCIe 4.0x4 host interface. Circuit-level validation via Spectre 19.1 (PTM-MG 14nm) with Monte Carlo V_TH mismatch and QLC drift modeling; accumulator synthesized with ASAP7 7nm at 1 GHz. Workloads: BEIR/NQ, HotpotQA, synthetic dataset (16GB-120GB); embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and all-mpnet-base-v2. Baselines: CPU-IVF (FAISS IVF-Flat on dual-socket 128-core server, 1.5TB DDR4), NSP baseline, REIS.
facts.limitations: Results are simulation-based (cycle-level SSD model plus Spectre/Monte Carlo circuit simulation), not measurements from fabricated silicon. Read latency/energy parameters are rescaled from prior measured NAND data (294.9 nJ/page read, 30us SLC / 140us QLC). Absolute end-to-end RAG serving latency (including LLM generation) is not reported; metrics focus on retrieval stage. Endurance/write-amplification impact of DTS sensing on QLC cells is not quantified in the visible evidence. DTS sensing resolution degrades at larger simultaneous-cell count m, a tradeoff tuned per config.
facts.project_relevance: D-NOVA is a NAND-centric in-storage compute design that pushes vector search into the flash array, directly relevant to whether 3D NAND can take on AI-serving storage-hierarchy roles (RAG retrieval) beyond bulk storage. For the project card it is a simulation-stage architecture study showing how in-array sensing can convert NAND density into retrieval throughput/energy gains; it is not a product or deployed system. The QLC-density-at-SLC-latency claim touches the storage-media density/bandwidth/latency questions.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.17538v1 (20 Jul 2026), to appear MICRO 2026; FETCHED primary source; authors from UC San Diego.
All performance numbers are simulation-based (cycle-level SSD simulator + Spectre/Monte Carlo), not silicon measurements.
Baselines explicitly named: CPU-IVF (FAISS on 128-core server), NSP near-storage processor, REIS in-storage; D-NOVA variants D-NOVA/D-NOVA-F/D-NOVA-XF differ by (m1,m2,m3) multi-cell sensing config.

facts.title: Kioxia and SanDisk 10th-Gen 332-Layer QLC NAND Achieves Industry's Highest Bit Density
facts.event_hint: Kioxia + SanDisk unveil 10th-generation 332-layer QLC 3D NAND at FMS 2026 (Aug 4, 2026): >37 Gb/mm^2 bit density (industry-leading claim), 4.8 Gb/s interface, CBA architecture.
facts.problem: AI training, inference and hyperscale datacenter workloads are driving rapid data-volume growth, putting pressure on storage to deliver higher capacity, higher performance and improved energy efficiency simultaneously. The release positions prior QLC 3D NAND generations as unable to meet this combined density+bandwidth+power envelope for next-generation AI/cloud infrastructure.
facts.mechanism: 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory with a 332-layer architecture and optimized floorplan. Built on CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) technology, which fabricates CMOS logic and the memory array on separate wafers in their optimized conditions and then bonds them with high-precision wafer-to-wafer alignment, enhancing density scaling, performance and manufacturing efficiency. The 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface is enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 plus the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol. Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency. The combination is claimed to deliver simultaneous gains in density, bandwidth and energy efficiency.

evidence.claim: The 332-layer architecture and optimized floorplan deliver up to a 60% increase in bit density, achieving >37 Gb/mm^2 compared to the 8th-generation, claimed as the industry benchmark for QLC NAND bit density.
evidence.condition: 10th-generation QLC 3D flash, 332-layer; Kioxia/SanDisk survey as of August 3, 2026
evidence.source_locator: Press release: Key 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory technology highlights (bulleted list)

evidence.claim: It is the industry's first QLC 3D flash memory technology to reach a 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface, enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 and the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol.
evidence.baseline: prior QLC 3D NAND interfaces (none had reached 4.8 Gb/s)
evidence.condition: 10th-gen QLC, Toggle DDR6.0 + SCA; 1Gb/s defined as 1,000,000,000 bits/s, value obtained under vendor-specific test environment, may vary with use conditions
evidence.source_locator: Press release: Key highlights (4.8 Gb/s interface bullet) and footnotes

evidence.claim: CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) architecture fabricates CMOS logic and the memory array on separate wafers before high-precision wafer-to-wafer bonding, enhancing density scaling, performance and manufacturing efficiency.
evidence.source_locator: Press release: Key highlights (CBA bullet) and footnote 2

evidence.claim: Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency, addressing power and cooling challenges of modern AI and cloud infrastructure.
evidence.baseline: prior-generation I/O data-out transfer power efficiency
evidence.source_locator: Press release: Key highlights (PI-LTT bullet) and narrative paragraph

evidence.claim: The new generation improves read and write bandwidth compared to the 8th-generation 3D flash memory (directional, no absolute throughput numbers disclosed).
evidence.source_locator: Press release: unveiling narrative paragraph

facts.evaluation_context: Source type: joint vendor press release from Kioxia Corporation and Sandisk Corporation, unveiled at the Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) 2026 conference, Santa Clara, CA, August 4, 2026. Product class: 10th-generation QLC (Quad-Level-Cell) 3D NAND flash, 332 layers, CBA architecture, Toggle DDR6.0 + SCA interface at 4.8 Gb/s, PI-LTT termination. Target applications stated: AI storage architectures, cloud platforms, data-intensive innovation, agent-based and physical AI. Comparison baseline: Kioxia/SanDisk's own 8th-generation 3D flash memory. 'Industry's highest'/'industry benchmark'/'industry's first' claims are based on Kioxia and SanDisk survey as of August 3, 2026.
facts.limitations: This is a product announcement press release, not a measured characterization paper. No quantitative P/E endurance, write amplification, random/sequential read-write throughput (IOPS/MB/s), access latency, $/bit, die size, or power draw figures are disclosed. The 4.8 Gb/s interface value is explicitly vendor-test-environment-specific and 'may vary depending on use conditions'. The 'up to 60%' density gain and 'improved read/write bandwidth' are directional and not given as absolute numbers. Mass-production / sampling / commercialization timing is not specified in the release (Kioxia CTO only says they 'will accelerate development toward commercialization'), so this is an announcement, not a shipping product. The 'industry's highest/first' benchmarks are self-surveyed as of Aug 3, 2026.
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to the storage-media card's question of whether NAND density/bandwidth/power evolution is crossing into system-usable territory for AI storage tiers: 332-layer QLC at >37 Gb/mm^2 with a 4.8 Gb/s interface is a concrete generational step that, combined with PI-LTT power-efficiency improvement, targets the AI/cloud capacity-per-watt envelope. However, the absence of endurance, latency and absolute throughput numbers means it cannot yet be judged whether this changes the storage hierarchy boundary (e.g., versus HBF or against persistent-memory tiers). It is best treated as a credible announcement signal pending characterization and a commercialization timeline. Verification gap: obtain P/E endurance, write amplification, measured random/sequential throughput, latency and mass-production schedule before treating it as a deployable capability.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the quantitative P/E endurance, write amplification, random and sequential read/write throughput (IOPS/MB/s), access latency, and die/die-stack physical dimensions for this 332-layer QLC device?
What is the sampling and mass-production timeline, and the target $/bit or $/GB, for the 10th-generation QLC products?

facts.title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
facts.event_hint: KAP (Knowledge Access Planning): a serving-time IR that compiles structured knowledge priors (e.g. GraphRAG) into a runtime access plan governing physical KV access, instantiated as GraphSpec on a vLLM backend.
facts.problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: knowledge-selection frontends (RAG, GraphRAG, HippoRAG) produce structured priors, but prompt serialization collapses them into a flat token stream, forcing the serving backend to densely consume the full KV state during decoding. Richer contexts enlarge the KV footprint and decode-time memory traffic, increasing latency and degrading throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of the context.
facts.mechanism: KAP elevates structured knowledge priors into first-class physical execution artifacts via a universal IR - the runtime access plan - which compiles knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training. GraphSpec is a compiler-executor instantiation connecting a Graph-RAG frontend to a vLLM backend; it produces a selected-KV proposal view with full-context verification. A phase-boundary cost model characterizes the positive-speedup regime (margin h-s between acceptance rate h and retained-KV ratio s).

evidence.claim: Across 4K-128K long-context QA, GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K (10.8% at 64K, 40.1% at 4K) while maintaining answer quality comparable to full-context decoding.
evidence.condition: long-context QA, Graph-RAG frontend, vLLM backend
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 2; PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: GraphSpec improves decode throughput (TPS) over full-context baseline by 1.08x at 4K-16K, 1.09x at 32K, 1.13x at 64K, and 1.19x at 128K; speedup grows with context length as retained-KV ratio falls.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 2

evidence.claim: Answer quality is preserved: GraphSpec pass rate differs from full-context baseline by at most 0.3 percentage points at five of six lengths, and is 1.9 points higher at 64K; average similarity closely matched across 4K-128K (e.g., 0.741 vs 0.748 at 64K).
evidence.condition: LLM-as-judge pass rate at 0.5 threshold; independent human audit 95% agreement on 100 SPIQA samples
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 3; PDF Page 12 - Table 1

evidence.claim: Ablation (64K): Physical concat (same selected evidence materialized as shortened 0.95K prompt) pass rate falls to 73.9% vs 87.9% for GraphSpec; Random concat 49.7%, Local window 47.1%, confirming the runtime access plan - not prompt shortening - is the operative bridge.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 14 - Table 4

evidence.claim: Phase-boundary model consistency (RQ4): retained ratio s decreases from 0.401 (4K) to 0.055 (128K) while acceptance h stays high (0.953-0.962), so margin h-s grows from 0.557 to 0.897 and measured speedup rises from 1.08x to 1.19x without refitting the cost model.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 14 - Table 5

facts.evaluation_context: Long-context QA workloads (4K-128K tokens) with a Graph-RAG knowledge-selection frontend and vLLM serving backend. Quality metric: LLM-as-judge similarity in [0,1] with 0.5 pass threshold (4 dimensions: fact consistency 40%, information completeness 30%, logical structure 20%, expression quality 10%), independently audited against 3-annotator majority vote on 100 SPIQA samples (95% agreement). Efficiency metrics: decode throughput (TPS) and TTFT; frontend retrieval excluded from TTFT (Graph-RAG evidence frozen before benchmarking). All serving-path measurements collected with diagnostic profiling disabled.
facts.limitations: Evaluation is limited to one KAP instantiation (GraphSpec with Graph-RAG frontend + vLLM backend); authors explicitly state empirical evidence does not exhaust the broader design space. Results are strongest for long-context QA where graph-derived priors ground in evidence spans; effectiveness for other frontends, plan compilers, access policies, or backends is unverified. TTFT is slightly worse for GraphSpec at several lengths (e.g., 1.56s vs 1.51s at 4K) because plan compilation and selected-KV materialization are included. No production deployment scale, GPU hardware spec, or cost data is reported in the visible evidence.
facts.project_relevance: KAP/GraphSpec is a serving-runtime/compiler optimization that reduces decode-time KV memory traffic by making structured knowledge priors executable - directly relevant to LLM serving efficiency and KV-cache management. It offers a concrete mechanism (runtime access plan IR) for decoupling physical KV consumption from prompt length. For the project card it is a research system evaluated on long-context QA, not a production deployment; its horizontal relevance is to inference serving rather than to the seven deep topics specifically.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.24260v1 (27 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from QiYuanLab.
Quality metric is LLM-as-judge (not human eval on all samples); independently audited on 100 SPIQA samples with 95% judge-human agreement.
Backend is vLLM; frontend is Graph-RAG; baselines are full-context vLLM, physical/random/local-window concat.
